## 17. CARD MODE ADDENDUM

output_mode is card_mode: the text fills a short card for a Manager / Strategic Decision Maker,
shown with four stat tiles and two dashboard panels (01: map of the 20 most geographically
sensitive LSOAs, coloured by rank, with the expert-highlighted regions; 02: all 168 LSOAs ranked
by GeoSensitivity). This section replaces section 14 "Length and form" and its bolding rule.
Every other section, including prohibited claims, the evidence-review "next step" rule and the
self-check, still applies.

Plain language for this reader: do not cite Moran's I, p-values, LISA class names, coefficients,
correlation values or other test statistics. GeoSensitivity values, ranks, shares, counts and
"N times" ratios are fine. GeoSensitivity means the model is sensitive to an area's own data;
never write that the model "relies on" or "depends on" an area. Name areas by locality; no
planner-style list of areas and no street names.

Return ONLY one JSON object with exactly these keys:

- "headline": one sentence, at most 20 words: the single most decision-relevant finding that
  answers user_question.
- "tiles": exactly 4 objects {"value": ..., "label": ...}. value is one figure from the
  evidence (at most 8 characters, e.g. "18/20", "46%"); label is at most 6 words saying what the
  figure is. Choose the four figures a manager should remember: one for the finding, one for
  the exception, two for confidence.
- "section_01": at most 70 words, finding and exception (panel 02): what the model mainly reads
  Hull through (manager_overview.finding), whether geographic sensitivity is widespread or
  concentrated (manager_overview.concentration), and the single exceptional area by locality
  name with its GeoSensitivity and how many times the next area it is.
- "section_02": at most 70 words, confidence and next step (panel 01): agreement with the
  expert regions against chance, whether the top 20 hold when neighbouring areas are added, and
  the across-model result (manager_overview.confidence.across_models.plain_reading). End with
  ONE evidence-review next step, never an operational action.
- "footer": one limitation, at most 15 words, ruling out causal or resourcing readings.

Key-term counts: 1-2 in the headline and 2-4 in EACH section. Tiles and footer carry no
markup.

Highlighting markup (you choose what to mark):

- wrap every figure you cite as [[n:...]], e.g. [[n:14%]];
- wrap the key terms a planner should catch when scanning as [[t:...]]. This is required,
  not optional: keep to the counts given above, each at most 4 words (the finding phrase
  itself, the leading feature names, or the key place names). Before answering, count the
  [[t:...]] spans and fix any count outside the range;
- no other markup and no markdown bold.

Every figure must be copied or rounded from EVIDENCE_JSON (shares as percentages:
0.139 -> 14%). Do not compute new figures and do not cite a figure that is not supplied.

ILLUSTRATIVE_NARRATIVE in the user message shows the expected structure, order, tone and
markup density. It is an example of wording, not evidence: take every figure from
EVIDENCE_JSON.

illustrative_narrative.headline: The model reads Hull through [[t:recent crime history]]; [[t:Old Town]] is the one exceptional area.
illustrative_narrative.section_01: The model reads Hull mainly through [[t:recent crime history]]: the six-month average leads in [[n:144]] of [[n:168]] areas. Geographic sensitivity is [[t:concentrated]]: the top [[n:20]] areas carry [[n:46%]] of the total effect. [[t:Old Town]] is the exception at [[n:22.33]], about [[n:3.1]] times Dairycoates, the next area.
illustrative_narrative.section_02: The results agree with [[t:local expertise]]: [[n:18]] of the [[n:20]] most sensitive areas lie in the expert's regions ([[n:90%]], against [[n:35%]] by chance), and all [[n:20]] stay when neighbouring areas are added. Across [[n:10]] models, higher accuracy did not bring closer expert agreement. [[t:Next step]]: review the evidence for Old Town before relying on rankings elsewhere.
illustrative_narrative.footer: Describes model sensitivity, not causes of crime or where to put resources.

global_geo.note: GeoSensitivity is the Geo-branch area-data SMILE coefficient: masking an LSOA replaces all of its model inputs with Hull training medians, and the coefficient attributes the resulting prediction shift to that LSOA. It is not latitude or longitude feature attribution.

global_spatial_pattern.note: LISA classes describe clustering of signed GeoSensitivity (area-data design). They are not crime hotspots and not latitude/longitude effects.
global_spatial_pattern.lisa_counts_unit: number of LSOAs in each LISA class, not number of clusters

evaluation.att_stability_note: Controlled-input ATT stability. Distinct from multi-run Consistency.

consistency.definition: Multi-run explanation consistency across seeds (consistency_seed_base=100). Pairwise Rank Spearman, Score Pearson, and Top-20% Jaccard of |coefficients|. Not controlled-input ATT stability.

geo_design.name: area_data
geo_design.definition: Area-data design: masking an LSOA replaces ALL of its model inputs with the training median; response is Wasserstein-1 on the affected LSOA-month predictions of the 30-feature model; LSOAs ranked by the signed Geo-SMILE coefficient.

limitations: No RAG / no invented local context.
pattern_scale is not established in the computed outputs.
local_p_adjusted is not available in the published LISA table.
evidence.user_question: What is the main city-wide finding, what is exceptional, can the results be trusted, and what evidence should be reviewed next?

concentration.note: single-area shift = prediction change when one LSOA's inputs are replaced by Hull medians

intervention_impact.note: supplementary diagnostic: masking the top 20 moves predictions more than masking 20 random areas

across_models.plain_reading: more accurate models did not reliably give closer agreement with the expert regions

manager_overview.limitation: Model sensitivity, not causes of crime, planning targets or a basis for resourcing.
